motif: switch pin approaching then seated in a hot-swap PCB socket
subject: Two mirrored panels of the same switch/socket pair on a warm-paper background. Left panel: switch housing hovering above the plate/PCB with metal contact pins stopping short of the socket, relaxed open contact leaves inside the socket housing, and a dashed alignment guide + motion chevron showing the intended drop path (captioned 'approach — contacts open'). Right panel: pins fully descended, coral spring-contact leaves bowed inward and gripping the pin shaft with filled contact-point dots and a soft glow halo at the contact depth (captioned 'seated — contact made'). A dashed rightward arrow labeled 'hot-swap' bridges the two panels. A lower-center callout, linked to both sockets by faint dashed leader lines, depicts a bent/kinked pin with a coral warning dot and the caption 'repeated swaps -> pin fatigue', visualizing the durability tradeoff against solder-free convenience. Left-margin labels (switch / socket / PCB) and a Newsreader-italic footer title anchor the family convention. Bronze theme dot at upper-right (1158, 42).
